Brief step 4 only ran `tests/test_glaze.py`. The completion contract needs the project's documented command, and CONTRIBUTING.md names `just verify` (linter, type checker, every test in `tests/`). So `task-done` runs that, and it writes the ledger line only if it passes.

No file edits are needed. `task-done` appends the ledger line itself, and there is nothing to ask first.

<command>
~/.claude/skills/executing-plans/scripts/task-done specs/plans/9-kiln-log.md 2 a9f3e21 -- just verify
</command>

If it passes, the ledger gets `Task 2: complete (commits a9f3e21..07d5c8b, tests: just verify → <result>)`. I then mark Task 2's todo complete and start Task 3:

<command>
~/.claude/skills/executing-plans/scripts/task-start specs/plans/9-kiln-log.md 3
</command>

If `just verify` fails, nothing is recorded and Task 2 stays open. I'd debug the cause with systematic-debugging, fix it, commit, and re-run `task-done`. If the plan was wrong, I'd ledger a `Task 2: Ruling:` line.

Message to my partner:

> Task 2: `tests/test_glaze.py` passed (6 passed), committed as `07d5c8b`. I'm running `just verify` from CONTRIBUTING.md as the task's closing gate and will record the result in the ledger. Moving straight on to Task 3.
